correctness.rationale: The subgroup graph is exactly the point-line projective-plane incidence graph with the line part completed to a clique. Degree separation forces type preservation and hence \(\operatorname{PGL}(3,p)\). For \(p=2\), only noncollinear point triples and their duals have trivial pointwise stabilizer. For odd \(p\), every triple has a surviving projectivity; four-vertex bases are exactly projective frames, their duals, triangle plus avoiding line, and the dual mixed class. Two-point/two-line sets always admit an elation or homology. The orbit and incidence counts sum to \(5|\operatorname{PGL}(3,p)|/12\). Exact \(p=2,3\) enumeration agrees.

value.rationale: The determining number is a standard symmetry invariant, and this result completely resolves it on the first projective-plane subgroup-intersection family rather than reporting a single base. The four odd-prime minimum-base types expose a real mixed incidence phenomenon: triangle-plus-avoiding-line bases coexist with ordinary projective frames, while every two-plus-two candidate fails by a perspectivity. The exact count gives a closed symmetry statistic and distinguishes the Fano boundary \(p=2\) from every odd prime.
